security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's TCG translation of SCBNDSRD incorrectly rounds the requested length DOWN (instead of correctly computing the largest representable length ≤ rs2) or fails to clear cd.tag when (a) cs1.tag=0, (b) cs1 is sealed, or (c) the computed bounds for cd exceed cs1's original bounds — any of these errors can produce a capability with bounds larger than the spec permits, enabling cross-trust-domain data exposure. Additionally, the instruction's operation section is marked 'TODO' in the spec, meaning the precise normative rounding algorithm is not yet frozen; QEMU must not implement this based on the non-normative NOTE describing a trailing-zero heuristic without formal algorithmic specification.
security_spec.summary: SCBNDSRD rounds capability bounds DOWN for representability to safely share buffers across trust domains; any rounding error, missed tag-clear condition, or premature implementation before the 'TODO' operation section is finalized can yield over-broad capabilities granting unauthorized cross-domain memory access

findings.finding: No SCBNDSRD/Zybndsrdw implementation exists in this QEMU repository. Searched all .c, .h, .inc, and .decode files across the entire codebase for SCBNDSRD, scbndsrd, ybndsrdw, cap_bounds_set, representable_length, bounds_round, and general CHERI/capability terms — zero matches. The CHERI RISC-V extension support lives in a downstream fork (github.com/CTSRD-CHERI/qemu) and has not been upstreamed into this repository. Since there is no emulation code to audit, there are no buggy TCG translations, no missing tag-clearing for sealed/invalid cs1, no incorrect bounds rounding, and no capability-trust-domain data exposure.

spec_citations.excerpt: Copy the capability from register cs1 to cd. Set the base address of its bounds to the value of cs1.address. Round _down_ the requested length ... Set cd.tag=0 if cs1.tag=0, cs1 is sealed or if cd's bounds exceed cs1's bounds.

This instruction is useful when exposing (byte) buffers across trust domains. ... Rounding the base _down_ and/or the length _up_ (as with SCBNDSR) risks exposing buffered data not suitable for exposure to the different trust domain.

[NOTE] — {SCBNDSRD} finds the largest length l that is both <= rs2 and precisely representable given base b. This value may be efficiently found, for most capability encoding schemes, by counting trailing zeros in the desired base address and computing the length that is a maximal mantissa shifted left by that count.
